description:
1. Recursively search /working for any regular file named "workspace" and save each matching absolute path, one per line, into '/tmp/found_workspace_paths.txt'.
2. Inspect '/tmp/found_workspace_paths.txt' and write a concise presence flag ('present' if the file contains entries, otherwise 'absent') to '/tmp/workspace_presence_flag.txt' to prepare for the final output.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Obtain a complete recursive listing of all filesystem entries under /working and save that listing to a file named "inventory.txt".
2. From "inventory.txt", extract entries that are regular files named "workspace", count those matches, and write the numeric count to a file named "workspace_count.txt" to prepare for the final presence check.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Recursively search the /working directory for any filesystem entries named "workspace" and record each match's absolute path and whether it is a regular file into a file named "matches.txt".
2. Read "matches.txt", determine if any recorded entry is a regular file, and write a single-line flag file "found_regular.txt" containing either yes or no to indicate presence for the final step.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Recursively record all filesystem entries under /working, including each entry's type and full path, into a file named "found_entries.txt" and confirm the record was saved.  
2. From "found_entries.txt", extract entries whose type indicates a regular (ordinary) file and whose base name is exactly "workspace", save all matching full paths to "matches.txt", and write the number of matches to "match_count.txt" to prepare for the final check.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
